Method: Config.is_rule_enabled(self, rule)  
Location: robocop/config.py → class Config  
Inputs: `rule` – an instance of `robocop.rules.Rule`. The method checks the rule’s enabled flag, its version compatibility, severity threshold and, after the recent change, also whether the rule is marked as deprecated.  
Outputs: `bool` – `True` if the rule is enabled for the current run; `False` if the rule is disabled, not compatible with the current Robot Framework version, below the severity threshold, or **deprecated** (deprecated rules are now treated as disabled).

Method: Rule.deprecation_warning(self)  
Location: robocop/rules.py → class Rule  
Inputs: none (uses the rule’s own attributes).  
Outputs: prints a warning message to stdout in the form:  
`Rule <severity><rule_id> <name> is deprecated. Remove it from your configuration.`  
Description: Emits the deprecation warning that the test suite captures when a deprecated rule is referenced in the configuration (via `include`, `exclude` or `configure`). The method is invoked by the `Config.is_rule_enabled` check and by the `Robocop` configuration handling.

+------------------------------------

+Some of our rules were deprecated and then removed in the past. It could lead to issues when jumping from older

+rules = {
+    "1102": Rule(rule_id="1102", name="custom-rule", msg="Example rule", deprecated=True, severity=RuleSeverity.ERROR),

future.pr_description:
Add mechanism for rule deprecation
Closes #1025 

Documentation visuals for deprecated rule could be improved but it can be done in the future updates - especially that we don't have any deprecated rule right now.
future.problem_statement:
Do not remove rules, only deprecate them
We had already removed some rules in the past (with some sort of deprecation period). In the future it will be better to 'move' rule to deprecation forever instead removing it. Our documentation will be more consistent (the rules will not 'dissapear' suddenly when switching between versions) and there will no sudden blank space in rules ids:

```
    "080X": Rule(
        rule_id="080X",

    ),
    "080X+1": Rule(
        rule_id="080X+1",
        deprecated=True,
    ),
    "080X+2": Rule(
        rule_id="080X+2",

    ),
```

If the rule is marked as deprecate, it will show warning when rule is used in --include/--exclude (same as with current deprecation solution but it will be handled on rule definition level, not on configuration level). The rule implementation could be removed.

+Robocop 2.7.0
+================
+
+You can install the latest available version by running::
+
+    pip install --upgrade robotframework-robocop
+
+or to install exactly this version::
+
+    pip install robotframework-robocop==2.7.0
+
+
+File configuration changes
+---------------------------
+
+We addressed several smaller issues and incoherence with Robocop file configuration.
+
+Overriding default configuration file
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+When you're using Robocop from the command line it reads both the cli arguments and default
+configuration file (found in the disk). The default configuration file (either ``.robocop`` or ``pyproject.toml`` file)
+is used as a base that can be overridden by the cli arguments. The problem with the previous implementation was
+that when user specified path to argument file in the cli::
+
+    robocop --argumentfile myconfig.txt
+
+Robocop would read both default configuration file and configuration file from ``--argumentfile``. Now it will read
+default configuration file only if ``-A / --argumentfile`` options are not used.

current.pr_description:
Refactor Config class to override default configuration file
Fixes #751

Now if user run:

```
robocop --verbose
```
it will use configuration from both cli and default configuration file (if it exists). This works like before.

When user run:

```
robocop --argumentfile path/to/file.txt
```
It will only use configuration from the cli and configuration file passed using ``--argumentfile`` (default configuration file will not be loaded).

Linux

2.5.0, 2.6.0

future.pr_description:
Deprecate unnecessary-string-conversion rule
Closes #986
future.problem_statement:
[Bug] Rule unnecessary-string-conversion is inherently bad
### What happened?

Hi,

`"${status}" == "200"` and `$status == 200` give different results in many cases and you can never know in which case they are equivalent. The situation is even worse when there is a less/greater-than operation instead of the equivalence (the rule applies even to these cases).



### What command/code did you try to run?

See the following test:
```
*** Keywords ***
Check Equal
    [Arguments]  ${value}
    ${match}  Set Variable  True
    IF  "${value}" == "1"
        ${match}  Set Variable  not ${match}
    END
    IF  $value == 1
        ${match}  Set Variable  not ${match}
    END
    Should Be True  ${match}  msg=Expressions do not match for value "${value}"

Check Greater Than
    [Arguments]  ${value}
    ${match}  Set Variable  True
    IF  "${value}" > "5"
        ${match}  Set Variable  not ${match}
    END
    IF  $value > 5
        ${match}  Set Variable  not ${match}
    END
    Should Be True  ${match}  msg=Expressions do not match for value "${value}"

*** Test Cases ***
Test 1
    Check Equal  1

Test 2
    Check Greater Than  6

Test 3
    Check Greater Than  40

Test 4
    Check Greater Than  ${40}
```

All the test cases fail, and that is for various causes. 
- When comparing two strings, you can be sure that they are comparable: they are of the same type. When you remove the string conversion, possibly different types of the two expressions come into play and the comparison can fail because of their mismatching types (as in Test 2 and Test 3). To be sure the two expressions are of compatibile types, you should employ dynamic analysis, I guess.
- Even if the two expressions are comparable without string conversion, their comparison with and without it do not need to yield the same results. In Test 1, `"1" == "1"`, but `"1" != 1` (because of different types, although values are equal). In Test 4, `40 > 5` but `"40" < "5"` (because of the different ways the things are ordered for various data types).

I am afraid it is very tedious or impossible to fix the rule or restrict it to cases when it is always correct, so that I suggest to delete it.

### Operating System

WIndows

### Robocop version

4.2.0

+Robocop 2.7.0
+================
+
+You can install the latest available version by running::
+
+    pip install --upgrade robotframework-robocop
+
+or to install exactly this version::
+
+    pip install robotframework-robocop==2.7.0
+
+
+File configuration changes
+---------------------------
+
+We addressed several smaller issues and incoherence with Robocop file configuration.
+
+Overriding default configuration file
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+When you're using Robocop from the command line it reads both the cli arguments and default
+configuration file (found in the disk). The default configuration file (either ``.robocop`` or ``pyproject.toml`` file)
+is used as a base that can be overridden by the cli arguments. The problem with the previous implementation was
+that when user specified path to argument file in the cli::
+
+    robocop --argumentfile myconfig.txt
+
+Robocop would read both default configuration file and configuration file from ``--argumentfile``. Now it will read
+default configuration file only if ``-A / --argumentfile`` options are not used.

current.pr_description:
Refactor Config class to override default configuration file
Fixes #751

Now if user run:

```
robocop --verbose
```
it will use configuration from both cli and default configuration file (if it exists). This works like before.

When user run:

```
robocop --argumentfile path/to/file.txt
```
It will only use configuration from the cli and configuration file passed using ``--argumentfile`` (default configuration file will not be loaded).

If default .robocop file exist, the another config file witch is set as  `--argumentfile` from command line, is ignored. So I can't execute robocop with other configurations if default .robocop file exist in main directory.

### Operating System

Linux

### Robocop version

2.5.0, 2.6.0

future.problem_statement:
Option to disable empty-variable rule for VAR and leave it for *** Variables *** section
Since new `VAR` syntax has by default the same settings as creating empty variables in `*** Variables ***` section, it is inconsistent with old `Create Dictionary` / `Create List` / `Set Variable` keywords that allowed creating empty variables with no need to use placeholders.

For example, this:
```robotframework
&{some_dict}    Create Dictionary  # no issues
```
with VAR and default for `empty-variable` rule is suggested to be refactored into this:
```robotframework
VAR    &{some_dict}    # now Robocop will complain
```

It seems inconsistent with previous way of creating empty variables inside of keywords. Maybe that suggestion is not necessarily bad but it would be nice-to-have feature to separate the setting for Variables section and for inline-created VARs.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/releasenotes/2.7.0.rst
@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+Robocop 2.7.0
+================
+
+You can install the latest available version by running::
+
+    pip install --upgrade robotframework-robocop
+
+or to install exactly this version::
+
+    pip install robotframework-robocop==2.7.0
+
+
+File configuration changes
+---------------------------
+
+We addressed several smaller issues and incoherence with Robocop file configuration.
+
+Overriding default configuration file
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+
+When you're using Robocop from the command line it reads both the cli arguments and default
+configuration file (found in the disk). The default configuration file (either ``.robocop`` or ``pyproject.toml`` file)
+is used as a base that can be overridden by the cli arguments. The problem with the previous implementation was
+that when user specified path to argument file in the cli::
+
+    robocop --argumentfile myconfig.txt
+
+Robocop would read both default configuration file and configuration file from ``--argumentfile``. Now it will read
+default configuration file only if ``-A / --argumentfile`` options are not used.

current.pr_description:
Refactor Config class to override default configuration file
Fixes #751

Now if user run:

```
robocop --verbose
```
it will use configuration from both cli and default configuration file (if it exists). This works like before.

When user run:

```
robocop --argumentfile path/to/file.txt
```
It will only use configuration from the cli and configuration file passed using ``--argumentfile`` (default configuration file will not be loaded).

[Bug] Providing `--argumentfile` is unuseful when default `.robocop` file exist
### What happened?

If default .robocop file exist, the another config file witch is set as  `--argumentfile` from command line, is ignored. So I can't execute robocop with other configurations if default .robocop file exist in main directory.

### Operating System

Linux

### Robocop version

2.5.0, 2.6.0

future.interface:
Method: Robocop.list_checkers(self)
Location: robocop/run.py, class Robocop
Inputs: self – Robocop instance whose `config.list` attribute is a string (either a glob pattern or the special keywords `"ENABLED"` / `"DISABLED"`). No other parameters.
Outputs: None (the method prints rule information to stdout and terminates the program by raising `SystemExit`).  
The method may raise `SystemExit` after emitting the list; no other exceptions are expected.
Description: Lists all available rules respecting the value of `self.config.list`. When the value is `"ENABLED"` or `"DISABLED"` it filters rules by their enabled status; otherwise it applies a glob pattern match. The output includes each rule with its ID, severity, name, description, and enabled/disabled marker, followed by a summary of rule counts, and then the program exits.

+List only enabled or disabled rules #764
+------------------------------------------
+
+Robocop can list all rules with ``--list`` option (or ``--list-configurables`` to only list rules that can be
+configured). Our every growing list of rules made the output of this command hard to read. That's why it is now
+possible to filter rules with ``ENABLED`` or ``DISABLED`` special patterns::
+
+    robocop --list ENABLED
+    robocop -i *doc* -i line-too-long --list ENABLED
+    robocop --exclude empty-lines-between-test-cases --list DISABLED
+    robocop --list-configurables ENABLED
+
+The new feature still coexist with existing feature that allows to filter list output using pattern::
+
+    robocop --list *line*
+
+However ``ENABLED``/``DISABLED`` patterns are more useful when you want to list only the rules that are enabled using
+your configuration.
+

+import os
+import re
+from functools import partial
+from pathlib import Path
+from urllib.parse import urlparse, urlunparse
+
+
+# Markdown regular expressions. Taken from the original Markdown.pl by John
+# Gruber, and modified to work in Python
+
+# Matches markdown links.
+# e.g. [scikit-learn](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn)
+MARKDOWN_LINK_REGEX = re.compile(
+    r'''
+        (                 # wrap whole match in $1
+          (?<!!)          # don't match images - negative lookbehind
+          \[
+            (             # link text = $2
+                [^\[\]]*  # not bracket
+                (?:
+                    \[[^\[\]]+\]  # another level of nested bracket with
+                                  # something inside
+                    [^\[\]]*      # not bracket
+                )*
+            )
+          \]
+          \(             # literal paren
+            [ \t]*
+            <?(.*?)>?    # href = $3
+            [ \t]*
+            (            # $4
+              (['"])     # quote char = $5
+              (.*?)      # Title = $6
+              \5         # matching quote
+            )?           # title is optional
+          \)
+        )
+    ''',
+    flags=re.VERBOSE,
+)
+
+# Matches markdown inline images.
+# e.g. ![alt-text](path/to/image.png)
+MARKDOWN_IMAGE_REGEX = re.compile(
+    r'''
+        (                # wrap whole match in $1
+          !\[
+            (.*?)        # alt text = $2
+          \]
+          \(             # literal paren
+            [ \t]*
+            <?(\S+?)>?   # src url = $3
+            [ \t]*
+            (            # $4
+              (['"])     # quote char = $5
+              (.*?)      # title = $6
+              \5         # matching quote
+              [ \t]*
+            )?           # title is optional
+          \)
+        )
+    ''',
+    flags=re.VERBOSE,
+)
+
+# Matches markdown link definitions.
+# e.g. [scikit-learn]: https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn
+MARKDOWN_LINK_DEFINITION_REGEX = re.compile(
+    r'''
+        ^[ ]{0,4}\[(.+)\]:   # id = $1
+        [ \t]*
+        \n?                # maybe *one* newline
+        [ \t]*
+        <?(\S+?)>?           # url = $2
+        [ \t]*
+        \n?                # maybe one newline
+        [ \t]*
+        (?:
+            (?<=\s)          # lookbehind for whitespace
+            ["(]
+            (.+?)            # title = $3
+            [")]
+            [ \t]*
+        )?                   # title is optional
+        (?:\n+|\Z)
+    ''',
+    flags=re.VERBOSE | re.MULTILINE,
+)
+
+
+def rewrite_relative_urls(
+    markdown: str, source_path: Path, destination_path: Path
+) -> str:
+    '''
+      Rewrites markdown so that relative links that were written at
+      source_path will still work when inserted into a file at destination_path
+    '''
+    def rewrite_url(url: str) -> str:
+        scheme, netloc, path, params, query, fragment = urlparse(url)
+
+        is_absolute = path.startswith('/')
+        if is_absolute:
+            return url
+
+        trailing_slash = path.endswith('/')
+
+        path = os.path.relpath(source_path.parent / path,
+                               destination_path.parent)
+
+        # ensure forward slashes are used, on Windows
+        path = Path(path).as_posix()
+
+        if trailing_slash:
+            # the above operation removes a trailing slash. Add it back if it
+            # was present in the input
+            path = path + '/'
+
+        return urlunparse((scheme, netloc, path, params, query, fragment))
+
+    def found_href(m: 're.Match', url_group_index=-1) -> str:
+        match_start, match_end = m.span(0)
+        href = m.group(url_group_index)
+        href_start, href_end = m.span(url_group_index)
+        rewritten_url = rewrite_url(href)
+        return (
+            m.string[match_start:href_start]
+            + rewritten_url
+            + m.string[href_end:match_end]
+        )
+
+    markdown = re.sub(
+        MARKDOWN_LINK_REGEX,
+        partial(found_href, url_group_index=3),
+        markdown
+    )
+    markdown = re.sub(
+        MARKDOWN_IMAGE_REGEX,
+        partial(found_href, url_group_index=3),
+        markdown
+    )
+    markdown = re.sub(
+        MARKDOWN_LINK_DEFINITION_REGEX,
+        partial(found_href, url_group_index=2),
+        markdown
+    )
+
+    return markdown

current.problem_statement:
Relative paths to images inside markdown are broken when doing an include
Hello @mondeja ! I haven't touched this module in over a year and as soon as you take it over, I have a feature request! :)

I'm including another section from our README into the docs. This section contains images, in the `![](path_to_image)` format. 

**README.md**
```md
....
<!--examples-start-->
![](docs/assets/example.png)
<!--examples-end-->
...
```

**docs/examples.md**
```md
{%
   include-markdown "../README.md"
   start="<!--examples-start-->"
   end="<!--examples-end-->"
%}
```

But the trouble is, when the snippet from README.md is included, the relative path breaks because it's relative to a different file. I guess the same problem would occur for relative hyperlinks, too.

I'm wondering about a flag that can be used on include-markdown, which would rewrite URLs to be relative to the inclusion location. So something like 
```md
{%
   include-markdown "../README.md"
   start="<!--examples-start-->"
   end="<!--examples-end-->"
   rewrite_relative_urls=true
%}
```

What do you think?

future.problem_statement:
Make heading-offset cumulative over nested inclusions
Use case is:

**File A.md**: 
```# A``` 

**File B.md**: 
```# B```

**File C.md**: 
```
#C

{%
include-markdown "./A.md"
heading-offset=1
%}

{%
include-markdown "./B.md"
heading-offset=1
%}
```
which is already rendered as following:

# C

## A

## B

But if you have
**File D.md**: 
```
# D

{%
include-markdown "./C.md"
heading-offset=1
%}
```

it is currently rendered as:

# D

## C

## # A

## # B

While I expected it to be rendered as follows:

# D

## C

### A

### B

Therefore, I suggest making **heading-offset** parameter cumulative over nested inclusions in order to achieve that expected result. Thank you for your feedback.

+import os
+import re
+from functools import partial
+from pathlib import Path
+from urllib.parse import urlparse, urlunparse
+
+
+# Markdown regular expressions. Taken from the original Markdown.pl by John
+# Gruber, and modified to work in Python
+
+# Matches markdown links.
+# e.g. [scikit-learn](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn)
+MARKDOWN_LINK_REGEX = re.compile(
+    r'''
+        (                 # wrap whole match in $1
+          (?<!!)          # don't match images - negative lookbehind
+          \[
+            (             # link text = $2
+                [^\[\]]*  # not bracket
+                (?:
+                    \[[^\[\]]+\]  # another level of nested bracket with
+                                  # something inside
+                    [^\[\]]*      # not bracket
+                )*
+            )
+          \]
+          \(             # literal paren
+            [ \t]*
+            <?(.*?)>?    # href = $3
+            [ \t]*
+            (            # $4
+              (['"])     # quote char = $5
+              (.*?)      # Title = $6
+              \5         # matching quote
+            )?           # title is optional
+          \)
+        )
+    ''',
+    flags=re.VERBOSE,
+)
+
+# Matches markdown inline images.
+# e.g. ![alt-text](path/to/image.png)
+MARKDOWN_IMAGE_REGEX = re.compile(
+    r'''
+        (                # wrap whole match in $1
+          !\[
+            (.*?)        # alt text = $2
+          \]
+          \(             # literal paren
+            [ \t]*
+            <?(\S+?)>?   # src url = $3
+            [ \t]*
+            (            # $4
+              (['"])     # quote char = $5
+              (.*?)      # title = $6
+              \5         # matching quote
+              [ \t]*
+            )?           # title is optional
+          \)
+        )
+    ''',
+    flags=re.VERBOSE,
+)
+
+# Matches markdown link definitions.
+# e.g. [scikit-learn]: https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn
+MARKDOWN_LINK_DEFINITION_REGEX = re.compile(
+    r'''
+        ^[ ]{0,4}\[(.+)\]:   # id = $1
+        [ \t]*
+        \n?                # maybe *one* newline
+        [ \t]*
+        <?(\S+?)>?           # url = $2
+        [ \t]*
+        \n?                # maybe one newline
+        [ \t]*
+        (?:
+            (?<=\s)          # lookbehind for whitespace
+            ["(]
+            (.+?)            # title = $3
+            [")]
+            [ \t]*
+        )?                   # title is optional
+        (?:\n+|\Z)
+    ''',
+    flags=re.VERBOSE | re.MULTILINE,
+)
+
+
+def rewrite_relative_urls(
+    markdown: str, source_path: Path, destination_path: Path
+) -> str:
+    '''
+      Rewrites markdown so that relative links that were written at
+      source_path will still work when inserted into a file at destination_path
+    '''
+    def rewrite_url(url: str) -> str:
+        scheme, netloc, path, params, query, fragment = urlparse(url)
+
+        is_absolute = path.startswith('/')
+        if is_absolute:
+            return url
+
+        trailing_slash = path.endswith('/')
+
+        path = os.path.relpath(source_path.parent / path,
+                               destination_path.parent)
+
+        # ensure forward slashes are used, on Windows
+        path = Path(path).as_posix()
+
+        if trailing_slash:
+            # the above operation removes a trailing slash. Add it back if it
+            # was present in the input
+            path = path + '/'
+
+        return urlunparse((scheme, netloc, path, params, query, fragment))
+
+    def found_href(m: 're.Match', url_group_index=-1) -> str:
+        match_start, match_end = m.span(0)
+        href = m.group(url_group_index)
+        href_start, href_end = m.span(url_group_index)
+        rewritten_url = rewrite_url(href)
+        return (
+            m.string[match_start:href_start]
+            + rewritten_url
+            + m.string[href_end:match_end]
+        )
+
+    markdown = re.sub(
+        MARKDOWN_LINK_REGEX,
+        partial(found_href, url_group_index=3),
+        markdown
+    )
+    markdown = re.sub(
+        MARKDOWN_IMAGE_REGEX,
+        partial(found_href, url_group_index=3),
+        markdown
+    )
+    markdown = re.sub(
+        MARKDOWN_LINK_DEFINITION_REGEX,
+        partial(found_href, url_group_index=2),
+        markdown
+    )
+
+    return markdown

current.problem_statement:
Relative paths to images inside markdown are broken when doing an include
Hello @mondeja ! I haven't touched this module in over a year and as soon as you take it over, I have a feature request! :)

I'm including another section from our README into the docs. This section contains images, in the `![](path_to_image)` format. 

**README.md**
```md
....
<!--examples-start-->
![](docs/assets/example.png)
<!--examples-end-->
...
```

**docs/examples.md**
```md
{%
   include-markdown "../README.md"
   start="<!--examples-start-->"
   end="<!--examples-end-->"
%}
```

But the trouble is, when the snippet from README.md is included, the relative path breaks because it's relative to a different file. I guess the same problem would occur for relative hyperlinks, too.

I'm wondering about a flag that can be used on include-markdown, which would rewrite URLs to be relative to the inclusion location. So something like 
```md
{%
   include-markdown "../README.md"
   start="<!--examples-start-->"
   end="<!--examples-end-->"
   rewrite_relative_urls=true
%}
```

What do you think?

+import os
+import re
+from functools import partial
+from pathlib import Path
+from urllib.parse import urlparse, urlunparse
+
+
+# Markdown regular expressions. Taken from the original Markdown.pl by John
+# Gruber, and modified to work in Python
+
+# Matches markdown links.
+# e.g. [scikit-learn](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn)
+MARKDOWN_LINK_REGEX = re.compile(
+    r'''
+        (                 # wrap whole match in $1
+          (?<!!)          # don't match images - negative lookbehind
+          \[
+            (             # link text = $2
+                [^\[\]]*  # not bracket
+                (?:
+                    \[[^\[\]]+\]  # another level of nested bracket with
+                                  # something inside
+                    [^\[\]]*      # not bracket
+                )*
+            )
+          \]
+          \(             # literal paren
+            [ \t]*
+            <?(.*?)>?    # href = $3
+            [ \t]*
+            (            # $4
+              (['"])     # quote char = $5
+              (.*?)      # Title = $6
+              \5         # matching quote
+            )?           # title is optional
+          \)
+        )
+    ''',
+    flags=re.VERBOSE,
+)
+
+# Matches markdown inline images.
+# e.g. ![alt-text](path/to/image.png)
+MARKDOWN_IMAGE_REGEX = re.compile(
+    r'''
+        (                # wrap whole match in $1
+          !\[
+            (.*?)        # alt text = $2
+          \]
+          \(             # literal paren
+            [ \t]*
+            <?(\S+?)>?   # src url = $3
+            [ \t]*
+            (            # $4
+              (['"])     # quote char = $5
+              (.*?)      # title = $6
+              \5         # matching quote
+              [ \t]*
+            )?           # title is optional
+          \)
+        )
+    ''',
+    flags=re.VERBOSE,
+)
+
+# Matches markdown link definitions.
+# e.g. [scikit-learn]: https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn
+MARKDOWN_LINK_DEFINITION_REGEX = re.compile(
+    r'''
+        ^[ ]{0,4}\[(.+)\]:   # id = $1
+        [ \t]*
+        \n?                # maybe *one* newline
+        [ \t]*
+        <?(\S+?)>?           # url = $2
+        [ \t]*
+        \n?                # maybe one newline
+        [ \t]*
+        (?:
+            (?<=\s)          # lookbehind for whitespace
+            ["(]
+            (.+?)            # title = $3
+            [")]
+            [ \t]*
+        )?                   # title is optional
+        (?:\n+|\Z)
+    ''',
+    flags=re.VERBOSE | re.MULTILINE,
+)
+
+
+def rewrite_relative_urls(
+    markdown: str, source_path: Path, destination_path: Path
+) -> str:
+    '''
+      Rewrites markdown so that relative links that were written at
+      source_path will still work when inserted into a file at destination_path
+    '''
+    def rewrite_url(url: str) -> str:
+        scheme, netloc, path, params, query, fragment = urlparse(url)
+
+        is_absolute = path.startswith('/')
+        if is_absolute:
+            return url
+
+        trailing_slash = path.endswith('/')
+
+        path = os.path.relpath(source_path.parent / path,
+                               destination_path.parent)
+
+        # ensure forward slashes are used, on Windows
+        path = Path(path).as_posix()
+
+        if trailing_slash:
+            # the above operation removes a trailing slash. Add it back if it
+            # was present in the input
+            path = path + '/'
+
+        return urlunparse((scheme, netloc, path, params, query, fragment))
+
+    def found_href(m: 're.Match', url_group_index=-1) -> str:
+        match_start, match_end = m.span(0)
+        href = m.group(url_group_index)
+        href_start, href_end = m.span(url_group_index)
+        rewritten_url = rewrite_url(href)
+        return (
+            m.string[match_start:href_start]
+            + rewritten_url
+            + m.string[href_end:match_end]
+        )
+
+    markdown = re.sub(
+        MARKDOWN_LINK_REGEX,
+        partial(found_href, url_group_index=3),
+        markdown
+    )
+    markdown = re.sub(
+        MARKDOWN_IMAGE_REGEX,
+        partial(found_href, url_group_index=3),
+        markdown
+    )
+    markdown = re.sub(
+        MARKDOWN_LINK_DEFINITION_REGEX,
+        partial(found_href, url_group_index=2),
+        markdown
+    )
+
+    return markdown

current.problem_statement:
Relative paths to images inside markdown are broken when doing an include
Hello @mondeja ! I haven't touched this module in over a year and as soon as you take it over, I have a feature request! :)

I'm including another section from our README into the docs. This section contains images, in the `![](path_to_image)` format. 

**README.md**
```md
....
<!--examples-start-->
![](docs/assets/example.png)
<!--examples-end-->
...
```

**docs/examples.md**
```md
{%
   include-markdown "../README.md"
   start="<!--examples-start-->"
   end="<!--examples-end-->"
%}
```

But the trouble is, when the snippet from README.md is included, the relative path breaks because it's relative to a different file. I guess the same problem would occur for relative hyperlinks, too.

I'm wondering about a flag that can be used on include-markdown, which would rewrite URLs to be relative to the inclusion location. So something like 
```md
{%
   include-markdown "../README.md"
   start="<!--examples-start-->"
   end="<!--examples-end-->"
   rewrite_relative_urls=true
%}
```

What do you think?

+import textwrap
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from mkdocs_include_markdown_plugin.process import rewrite_relative_urls
+
+
+def test_relative_link():
+    input = '''
+        Here's a [link](CHANGELOG.md) to the changelog.
+    '''
+    output = rewrite_relative_urls(input, Path('README'), Path('docs/nav.md'))
+    assert output == '''
+        Here's a [link](../CHANGELOG.md) to the changelog.
+    '''
+
+
+def test_multiline_link():
+    input = '''
+        Here's a [link whose text is really long and so is broken across
+        multiple lines](CHANGELOG.md) to the changelog.
+    '''
+    output = rewrite_relative_urls(input, Path('README'), Path('docs/nav.md'))
+    assert output == '''
+        Here's a [link whose text is really long and so is broken across
+        multiple lines](../CHANGELOG.md) to the changelog.
+    '''
+
+
+def test_relative_link_down():
+    input = '''
+        Check [this link](foobar.md) for more information
+    '''
+    output = rewrite_relative_urls(

+        Path('docs/setup.md')
+    )
+    assert output == '''

+    '''
+
+
+def test_link_with_hash():
+    input = '''
+        Here's a [link](CHANGELOG.md#v1.2.3) to the changelog.
+    '''

+    def find_match_in(self, typ, pattern):
+        """
+        Find a message with the given pattern among the stored messages.
+
+        Raises an exception if a message with the given pattern isn't found.
+
+        Parameters
+        ----------
+        typ : str
+            Type of messages ('error', 'warning', 'info') to be searched.
+
+        pattern : str
+            The pattern to match.

Added timing to output from Problem checks
### Summary

Added timing to the output from Problem checks, e.g.

```
INFO: checking all_unserializable_options...
INFO:     all_unserializable_options check complete (0.000095 sec).
INFO: checking auto_ivc_warnings...
INFO:     auto_ivc_warnings check complete (0.000002 sec).
[...]
INFO: checking unconnected_inputs...
WARNING: The following inputs are not connected:
  x (comp1.x)

INFO:     unconnected_inputs check complete (0.000082 sec).
```

Note that the issue suggests moving a certain check "to our standard checks".  The check this seems to be referring to (`_check_discrete_dependance`) is run during the construction of a `_TotalJacInfo` object, which is not done as part of `Problem` `setup` or `final_setup` when the standard checks are performed.   (`_TotalJacInfo` objects are created on demand when computing or checking total derivatives).  Therefore, this check has not been moved or modified in this PR.

### Related Issues

- Resolves #3274

future.problem_statement:
Add ability to return a copy with get_val
### Desired capability or behavior.

Depending on the options passed, get_val may currently return a view into an internal OpenMDAO vector.
This can have some unexpected behavior when repeatedly using set_val/get val when interrogating a system.

The simple workaround is to use `np.copy(prob.get_val(...))`, but its not obvious that users may need to do this.
We should add an argument `copy=False` by default.  This will be slightly less verbose for the user, and its presence in the options will document that it is sometimes necessary for users to use.

There's some argument to be made that copying should be the default behavior, but leaving it False for now will maintain backwards compatibility.

### Associated POEM

_No response_

future.pr_description:
Fixed inconsistency in forwarding params in Context.forward
`Context.forward` uses `Context.params` to fill in the options and passes the `kwargs` to `Context.invoke` which creates a new `Context` for the sub-command but doesn't pass the params to the new `Context` nor does it remove unused `kwargs`.

From the example mentioned in the [issue](https://github.com/pallets/click/issues/1568), now a union of params from the context and sub-context will be forwarded. 

For e.g. - If `command_1` has options `a and b` and `command_2` has options `a and c`, command_1 forwards to command_2, then `command_2` will receive `a, b and c` as `kwargs`. 

I was unsure whether or not to remove the unused options, so I've kept them for now. 

- fixes #1568

future.pr_description:
detect type from flag_value
If `type` is not given and the option is a flag, the type is detected from `flag_value` instead of falling back to `STRING`. This works even if `default=True` is given for feature flags, which simplifies `convert_type` a bit.

For 8.1, a further change to consider is for `convert_type` to return `UNPROCESSED` instead of `STRING` if the type was guessed from the default value. In that case, what should really happen is that a custom `type` should have been provided that would recognize/return the value in `default`, but converting it to `STRING` isn't correct either.

```python
import click

@click.command()
@click.option("--answer", flag_value=42)
def main(answer):

if __name__ == '__main__':

Click 8.0.0 `group.add_command(..)` does not replace name in description and when looking up defaults
With click 8.0.0 `click.group.add_command(..)` changed the behavior in how new command names are used:
Both the help text for the command as well as when looking up default values in `default_map` the previous command name instead of the one added by the group are shown.

Minimal example:

```
# test.py
import click

@click.command()
@click.option(
    "--qux",
    required=True
)
def foo(qux):
    print(qux)

@click.group()
def group():
    pass

group.add_command(foo, "bar")

group(default_map={"bar": {"qux": "val"}})
```
Run the above:
* with click 7.x: 
> $ python3 test.py bar --help
> Usage: test.py bar [OPTIONS]
> // and
> $ python3 test.py bar
> val
* with click 8.0.0:
> $ python3 test.py bar --help
> Usage: test.py foo [OPTIONS]
> // and
> $ python3 test.py bar
> Usage: test.py foo [OPTIONS]
> Try 'test.py foo --help' for help.
>
> Error: Missing option '--qux'.

I would have expected that both the help shows the name of the command as "bar" (as using "foo" will result in an error)
and the lookup for the default using "bar" as a key.

Environment:

- Python version: 3.9.5
- Click version: 8.0.0

show help text with invalid default

```

future.pr_description:
expand patterns in Windows args
On Windows, if a command is called from the command line (so it uses `sys.argv`), globs, user dir, and env vars will be expanded. Uses `glob.glob`, `os.path.expanduser`, and `os.path.expandvars`. On Unix shells it is left to the shell to handle expansion, but Windows cmd.exe and powershell don't do expansion, so Click will handle it. `**` recursive expansion is enabled.

Inputs: 
- **password** – the plaintext password to hash.  
- **method** – a string selecting the key‑derivation function. Supported values are `"pbkdf2"` (optionally followed by `":hash_name[:iterations]"`) and `"scrypt"` (optionally followed by `":n:r:p"`). The default is the PBKDF2 variant with SHA‑256 and 600 000 iterations.  
- **salt_length** – length of the random salt to generate; must be a positive integer (ValueError raised for ≤ 0).  
Outputs: A single string of the form ``"{actual_method}${salt}${hash}"`` where ``actual_method`` is the resolved method identifier (e.g. ``"pbkdf2:sha256:600000"`` or ``"scrypt:32768:8:1"``). The string can be stored and later passed to ``check_password_hash``.  
Description: Securely hashes a password using the selected KDF, automatically generating a random salt. The resulting string encodes the method, salt, and derived hash, enabling later verification.

Function: check_password_hash(pwhash: str, password: str) -> bool
Location: werkzeug.security module
Inputs: 
- **pwhash** – a hash string produced by ``generate_password_hash`` (``"{method}${salt}${hash}"``).  
- **password** – the plaintext password to verify against the stored hash.  
Outputs: ``True`` if the derived hash matches the stored hash; ``False`` for a mismatch or if ``pwhash`` is malformed (does not contain two ``$`` separators).  
Description: Validates a password by re‑deriving the hash using the method and salt embedded in ``pwhash`` and performing a constant‑time comparison. It supports the ``pbkdf2`` and ``scrypt`` methods introduced in the recent changes.

current.problem_statement:
support scrypt, deprecate basic hash methods
Scrypt provides much stronger security than PBKDF2. It also has the advantage of not needing to update parameters as often. It is in the standard library. @alex and @reaperhulk recommended `n=2**15, r=8, p=1` for parameters.

Additionally, insecure/basic methods need to be deprecated. Currently, the `plain` method is allowed, which just returns the password as-is. Additionally, plain hashes are supported, rather than always requiring a KDF, and any hash provided by `hashlib` is supported. Deprecate everything except `scrypt` and `pbkdf2`.

If projects notice they are using these old methods, they'll need to implement a migration strategy to upgrade their hashes.

future.pr_description:
fail on Python's extended int/float syntax
Python's `int` and `float` allow a leading plus `+123`, underscore separators `1_12`, and non-ASCII decimal digits `🯱🯲🯳`. `float` additionally allows no number before the decimal `.123`. None of these are valid when parsing HTTP header values. Use a regex to quickly check if the value is a "plain" int or float, raising `ValueError` if not. fixes #2716
future.problem_statement:
Improper Content-Length Parsing
## Description
werkzeug currently parses Content-Length using `int`. This causes problems because `int` accepts a lot more than should be acceptable in that field. The biggest problem characters are, '-', '+', and '_'.

# Examples
## HTTP requests in which werkzeug misinterprets content-length (assume all newlines are CRLF):

### Underscore between digits
```
GET / HTTP/1.1
Connection: close
Host: whatever
Content-Length: 0_1


```

### Plus sign prefix
```
GET / HTTP/1.1
Connection: close
Host: whatever
Content-Length: +1


```

# Solution
The set of things you want to accept in a Content-Length header is not equal to the set of things that can get through `int` without error. During Content-Length parsing, check that the value is all ASCII digits before accepting. A more principled approach would reject all invalid Content-Length fields instead of just ignoring them. This is the approach taken by a large majority of other HTTP servers.

# Versions
CPython version: 3.10.11
werkzeug version: main

current.problem_statement:
support scrypt, deprecate basic hash methods
Scrypt provides much stronger security than PBKDF2. It also has the advantage of not needing to update parameters as often. It is in the standard library. @alex and @reaperhulk recommended `n=2**15, r=8, p=1` for parameters.

Additionally, insecure/basic methods need to be deprecated. Currently, the `plain` method is allowed, which just returns the password as-is. Additionally, plain hashes are supported, rather than always requiring a KDF, and any hash provided by `hashlib` is supported. Deprecate everything except `scrypt` and `pbkdf2`.

If projects notice they are using these old methods, they'll need to implement a migration strategy to upgrade their hashes.

current.problem_statement:
support scrypt, deprecate basic hash methods
Scrypt provides much stronger security than PBKDF2. It also has the advantage of not needing to update parameters as often. It is in the standard library. @alex and @reaperhulk recommended `n=2**15, r=8, p=1` for parameters.

Additionally, insecure/basic methods need to be deprecated. Currently, the `plain` method is allowed, which just returns the password as-is. Additionally, plain hashes are supported, rather than always requiring a KDF, and any hash provided by `hashlib` is supported. Deprecate everything except `scrypt` and `pbkdf2`.

If projects notice they are using these old methods, they'll need to implement a migration strategy to upgrade their hashes.

future.pr_description:
cookie sets `Path=/` by default again
If the path parameter is not present, RFC 6265 has a rule for picking a `default-path` that's the parent of the current path. For some reason, Firefox and Chrome on my computer always pick `/` instead, which is why I thought it was ok to remove. This PR restores the previous behavior. Setting `Path=/` is also a requirement for the `__Host-` and `__Secure-` [cookie prefixes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Set-Cookie#cookie_prefixes).

fixes #2672
future.problem_statement:
`set_cookie` will no longer set path by default
It seems that since version 2.3.0 of Werkzeug the behaviour of `set_cookie` has changed. The documentation of the method says that by default the cookie will span the whole domain. In older versions this was true: if the parameter `path` was not set it defaulted to `"/"`. Now it defaults to `None`, which leads to `Path` being omitted in the `Set-Cookie` part of the header in the response sent to the client. The browser (tested with Firefox) seems then to just take the path from the request URL.

```
# return from an endpoint like /cookie/set
response.set_cookie('test_cookie', cookie_payload, expires=exp_in_thirty_minutes, secure=True,
                        samesite='Strict')
# --> cookie for client will have path set to /cookie
```

Expected is that `Path` of the cookie will be set to "/" according to the documentation of `set_cookie`.

Environment:

- Python version: 3.10
- Werkzeug version: 2.3.1

current.problem_statement:
support scrypt, deprecate basic hash methods
Scrypt provides much stronger security than PBKDF2. It also has the advantage of not needing to update parameters as often. It is in the standard library. @alex and @reaperhulk recommended `n=2**15, r=8, p=1` for parameters.

Additionally, insecure/basic methods need to be deprecated. Currently, the `plain` method is allowed, which just returns the password as-is. Additionally, plain hashes are supported, rather than always requiring a KDF, and any hash provided by `hashlib` is supported. Deprecate everything except `scrypt` and `pbkdf2`.

If projects notice they are using these old methods, they'll need to implement a migration strategy to upgrade their hashes.

Authorization.from_header with "Token" scheme cannot handle base64 padding on tokens
# Steps to reproduce

```
import base64
from werkzeug.datastructures.auth import Authorization
token = base64.encodebytes(b"This has base64 padding").decode("utf-8").strip()
a = Authorization.from_header(f"Token {token}")
a.token
```

# Expected result

```
VGhpcyBoYXMgYmFzZTY0IHBhZGRpbmc=
```

Location: Defined in pennylane/ops/functions/equal.py as a registered overload of qml.equal for HilbertSchmidt objects.
Inputs:
- **op1**, **op2**: Instances of qml.HilbertSchmidt whose equality is being evaluated.
- **check_interface**: If True, the function verifies that the underlying numerical interface (e.g., NumPy, JAX, Torch) of the parameters matches between the two ops.
- **check_trainability**: If True, the function checks that the requires_grad status of each parameter pair is the same.
- **rtol**, **atol**: Relative and absolute tolerances used for qml.math.allclose when comparing the data arrays of the two ops.
Outputs:
- Returns True if all of the following hold:
  1. Parameter data arrays are element‑wise close within the given tolerances.
  2. (When check_trainability is True) Corresponding parameters have identical requires_grad status.
  3. (When check_interface is True) Corresponding parameters share the same interface.
  4. The v_wires hyperparameters are exactly equal.
  5. The u_tape and v_tape hyperparameters are considered equal by qml.equal (using the same check flags and tolerances).
  6. The v_function hyperparameters are identical objects.

Description: This overload implements logical equality for qml.HilbertSchmidt operations. [BUG] `qml.equal` does not work with `qml.HilbertSchmidt`
### Expected behavior

Equal ops are detected to be equal

### Actual behavior

Equal ops are reported to be different

### Additional information

The culprit is `v_tape` in the hyperparameters.

### Source code

```shell
u_tape = qml.tape.QuantumScript([qml.Hadamard(0)])
v_function = lambda params: qml.RZ(params[0], wires=1)
v_params = np.array([0.6])
op1 = qml.HilbertSchmidt(v_params, v_wires=[1], u_tape=u_tape, v_function=v_function)
op2 = qml.HilbertSchmidt(v_params, v_wires=[1], u_tape=u_tape, v_function=v_function)

qml.equal(op1, op2)
```


### Tracebacks

```shell
False
```


### System information

```shell
pl dev
```

- [X] I have searched existing GitHub issues to make sure the issue does not already exist.

Inputs:
- **op1**, **op2**: Instances of qml.HilbertSchmidt whose equality is being evaluated.

- **check_trainability**: If True, the function checks that the requires_grad status of each parameter pair is the same.

Outputs:
- Returns True if all of the following hold:
  1. Parameter data arrays are element‑wise close within the given tolerances.
  2. (When check_trainability is True) Corresponding parameters have identical requires_grad status.
  3. (When check_interface is True) Corresponding parameters share the same interface.
  4. The v_wires hyperparameters are exactly equal.
  5. The u_tape and v_tape hyperparameters are considered equal by qml.equal (using the same check flags and tolerances).
  6. The v_function hyperparameters are identical objects.

current.problem_statement:
[BUG] `qml.equal` does not work with `qml.HilbertSchmidt`
### Expected behavior

Equal ops are detected to be equal

### Actual behavior

Equal ops are reported to be different

### Additional information

The culprit is `v_tape` in the hyperparameters.

### Source code

```shell
u_tape = qml.tape.QuantumScript([qml.Hadamard(0)])
v_function = lambda params: qml.RZ(params[0], wires=1)
v_params = np.array([0.6])
op1 = qml.HilbertSchmidt(v_params, v_wires=[1], u_tape=u_tape, v_function=v_function)
op2 = qml.HilbertSchmidt(v_params, v_wires=[1], u_tape=u_tape, v_function=v_function)

qml.equal(op1, op2)
```

future.pr_description:
Allow tuple-valued `control_values` with `qml.ctrl` on a `Controlled` instance.
**Context:**
By default, `control_values` of `Controlled` instances are lists.
`qml.defer_measurements` passes a tuple as `control_values` to `ctrl`.
`create_controlled_op`, called by `ctrl`, tries to merge `control_values` of the base operation and the provided `control_values`. 
The consequence is an attempted addition of `list` and `tuple`, if `qml.defer_measurements` hits a `qml.cond` of a `Controlled` instance, leading to #5717 

**Description of the Change:**
This PR fixes the above problem in two (redundant!) ways: 
- tuples are allowed to be passed as `control_values` to `ctrl`, which casts them to a `list`.
- `defer_measurements` passes a `list` itself.

Clearly those changes are redundant for the bug #5717, with the former also providing users with the option of using `tuple`s for `control_values`. We could skip the change to `defer_measurements`, thus.

Function: _equal_hilbert_schmidt(op1: qml.HilbertSchmidt, op2: qml.HilbertSchmidt, check_interface: bool = True, check_trainability: bool = True, rtol: float = 1e-5, atol: float = 1e-9) -> bool
Location: Defined in pennylane/ops/functions/equal.py as a registered overload of qml.equal for HilbertSchmidt objects.
Inputs:
- **op1**, **op2**: Instances of qml.HilbertSchmidt whose equality is being evaluated.
- **check_interface**: If True, the function verifies that the underlying numerical interface (e.g., NumPy, JAX, Torch) of the parameters matches between the two ops.
- **check_trainability**: If True, the function checks that the requires_grad status of each parameter pair is the same.
- **rtol**, **atol**: Relative and absolute tolerances used for qml.math.allclose when comparing the data arrays of the two ops.
Outputs:
- Returns True if all of the following hold:
  1. Parameter data arrays are element‑wise close within the given tolerances.
  2. (When check_trainability is True) Corresponding parameters have identical requires_grad status.
  3. (When check_interface is True) Corresponding parameters share the same interface.
  4. The v_wires hyperparameters are exactly equal.
  5. The u_tape and v_tape hyperparameters are considered equal by qml.equal (using the same check flags and tolerances).
  6. The v_function hyperparameters are identical objects.
- Returns False otherwise.
Description: This overload implements logical equality for qml.HilbertSchmidt operations. It extends the generic qml.equal function by comparing both the numeric data (with optional tolerance, interface, and trainability checks) and the relevant hyperparameters that define a Hilbert–Schmidt subroutine (u‑tape, v‑tape, v‑wires, and the v‑function). It is used by the test suite to verify that two HilbertSchmidt instances are considered equal only when all computational and structural aspects match.

current.problem_statement:
[BUG] `qml.equal` does not work with `qml.HilbertSchmidt`

Equal ops are detected to be equal

### Actual behavior

Equal ops are reported to be different

### Additional information

The culprit is `v_tape` in the hyperparameters.

### Source code

```shell

v_function = lambda params: qml.RZ(params[0], wires=1)
v_params = np.array([0.6])
op1 = qml.HilbertSchmidt(v_params, v_wires=[1], u_tape=u_tape, v_function=v_function)
op2 = qml.HilbertSchmidt(v_params, v_wires=[1], u_tape=u_tape, v_function=v_function)

qml.equal(op1, op2)
```

future.pr_description:
fix sum hash issue

**Context:**

`Sum.hash` uses `frozenset` to calculate the hash in an order independent way.  The problem is that `frozenset` ignores the fact that some operations may occur multiple times in the sum.  This leads to an incorrect hash.

The bad hash then propagated to incorrect `eigvals` and `diagonalizing_gates`

**Description of the Change:**

Uses `collections.Counter` to count how many times the operations occur.

**Benefits:**

Correct answers.

**Possible Drawbacks:**

speed.

**Related GitHub Issues:**


Fixes #5849 [sc-65903]

### Expected behavior

Given some circuit like this,

```
dev = qml.device("default.qubit", wires=3)

@qml.qnode(dev)
def circuit_separated():
    qml.RX(np.pi / 3, 0)
    qml.RZ(np.pi / 3, 0)

You expect the summed version to be
```
dev = qml.device("default.qubit", wires=3)

@qml.qnode(dev)
def circuit_summed():
    qml.RX(np.pi / 3, 0)
    qml.RZ(np.pi / 3, 0)
    return [
        qml.var(qml.Z(0) + qml.X(0))
    ]

>>> circuit_summed()
[tensor(0.75+0.4375, requires_grad=True)]
```

Furthermore,
When changing the circuit you expect the answer to change

```

    qml.RX(np.pi / 3, 0)
    qml.RZ(np.pi / 3, 0)

    ]

>>> circuit_summed()
# should be some new answer

    qml.RZ(np.pi / 3, 0)
    return [
        qml.var(qml.Z(0) + qml.X(0))
    ]

circuit_summed()
>>> [tensor(0.4375, requires_grad=True)] # That's odd

    ]

>>> circuit_summed()
[tensor(0.4375, requires_grad=True)] # That's odd, it's still the same answer!

Function: _equal_hilbert_schmidt(op1: qml.HilbertSchmidt, op2: qml.HilbertSchmidt, check_interface: bool = True, check_trainability: bool = True, rtol: float = 1e-5, atol: float = 1e-9) -> bool
Location: Defined in pennylane/ops/functions/equal.py as a registered overload of qml.equal for HilbertSchmidt objects.
Inputs:
- **op1**, **op2**: Instances of qml.HilbertSchmidt whose equality is being evaluated.
- **check_interface**: If True, the function verifies that the underlying numerical interface (e.g., NumPy, JAX, Torch) of the parameters matches between the two ops.
- **check_trainability**: If True, the function checks that the requires_grad status of each parameter pair is the same.
- **rtol**, **atol**: Relative and absolute tolerances used for qml.math.allclose when comparing the data arrays of the two ops.
Outputs:
- Returns True if all of the following hold:
  1. Parameter data arrays are element‑wise close within the given tolerances.
  2. (When check_trainability is True) Corresponding parameters have identical requires_grad status.
  3. (When check_interface is True) Corresponding parameters share the same interface.
  4. The v_wires hyperparameters are exactly equal.
  5. The u_tape and v_tape hyperparameters are considered equal by qml.equal (using the same check flags and tolerances).
  6. The v_function hyperparameters are identical objects.
- Returns False otherwise.
Description: This overload implements logical equality for qml.HilbertSchmidt operations. It extends the generic qml.equal function by comparing both the numeric data (with optional tolerance, interface, and trainability checks) and the relevant hyperparameters that define a Hilbert–Schmidt subroutine (u‑tape, v‑tape, v‑wires, and the v‑function). It is used by the test suite to verify that two HilbertSchmidt instances are considered equal only when all computational and structural aspects match.

[BUG] `null.qubit` no longer plays nicely with custom operations
### Expected behavior

``` py
import pennylane as qml
from pennylane.resource.error import ErrorOperation

class IssueErrorOp(ErrorOperation):
    def __init__(self, phase, wires):
        self.phase = phase
        super().__init__(phase, wires=wires)
    def error(self):
        return 1.0

@qml.qnode(qml.device('null.qubit', wires=2))
def circuit():
    IssueErrorOp(1.0, [0])
    return qml.state()

>>> circuit()
[0.0]
```

`null.qubit` should allow for adding custom operators to the workflow.

### Actual behavior

``` py
import pennylane as qml
from pennylane.resource.error import ErrorOperation

class IssueErrorOp(ErrorOperation):
    def __init__(self, phase, wires):
        self.phase = phase
        super().__init__(phase, wires=wires)
    def error(self):
        return 1.0

@qml.qnode(qml.device('null.qubit', wires=2))
def circuit():
    IssueErrorOp(1.0, [0])
    return qml.state()

>>> circuit()
DeviceError: Operator ReplyErrorOp(1.0, wires=[0]) not supported on null.qubit and does not provide a decomposition.
```

This issue exists on the master and possibly comes from using `DefaultQubit`'s `preprocess` for `null.qubit` as well.

current.pr_description:
#813 get t_eval from data
# Description
When using the `Simulation` class with the current provided as data (i..e drive cycles) `solve` now sets `t_eval` (if it isn't provided) to be the times in the data (non-dimensionlised). If `t_eval` is provided, `solve` checks that it contains all of the points in the data, and raises a warning if it doesn't. Maybe this should raise an actual exception to be totally fool proof, but there may be cases where people only want the solution returned at a subset of points. Happy for input on this. I think if people are solving in the long-winded way (i.e. not using `Simulation`) then we should just trust them to pick `t_eval` appropriately. 

Fixes #813

current.problem_statement:
fix t_eval to data for drive cycles
when simulating drive cycles the solvers work if `t_eval` is the same as the times provided in the data. when solving we should check if the current function has "[current data]" and then force the solve times to be those in the data (with a warning message that the solver is fixing t_eval). see below example

```
#
# Simulate drive cycle loaded from csv file
#
import pybamm
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import os

# load model
pybamm.set_logging_level("INFO")
model = pybamm.lithium_ion.DFN()

# create geometry
geometry = model.default_geometry

# get drive cycle data
cycle_name = "US06"
drive_cycle = pd.read_csv(
    os.path.join(pybamm.root_dir(), "input", "drive_cycles", cycle_name+".csv"),
    comment="#",
    skip_blank_lines=True
)
time_dim = drive_cycle.values[:, 0]
current_dim = drive_cycle.values[:, 1]

# load parameter values and process model and geometry
param = model.default_parameter_values
param["Current function [A]"] = "[current data]" + cycle_name
param.process_model(model)
param.process_geometry(geometry)

# set mesh
var = pybamm.standard_spatial_vars
var_pts = {var.x_n: 11, var.x_s: 11, var.x_p: 11, var.r_n: 5, var.r_p: 5}
mesh = pybamm.Mesh(geometry, model.default_submesh_types, var_pts)

# discretise model
disc = pybamm.Discretisation(mesh, model.default_spatial_methods)
disc.process_model(model)

# get dimensionless times for evaluation
tau = param.evaluate(pybamm.standard_parameters_lithium_ion.tau_discharge)
t_eval = time_dim / tau  # this works
# t_eval = np.linspace(0, 600 / tau, 600)  # this fails

# simulate US06 drive cycle
solver = pybamm.CasadiSolver(mode="fast")
solution = solver.solve(model, t_eval)

# plot
plot = pybamm.QuickPlot(solution)
plot.dynamic_plot()
```

Note that this works with Casadi in "fast" mode!

Issue 992 plot arrays
# Description
Added basic plots for 1D and 2D arrays (`pybamm.plot` and `pybamm.plot2D`). I've left these as separate methods, but I guess they could be combined and the appropriate plot called depending on what arrays you pass. On the other hand, maybe it is better to be explicit.

Method: Simulation.solve(self, t_eval=None, solver=None, external_variables=None)
Location: pybamm/simulation.py
Inputs:
- **t_eval** (array‑like or None): optional array of nondimensional times at which the solution is requested. If None and the parameter *"Current function [A]"* is supplied via data (i.e., a tuple ``(filename, data)``), the method automatically uses the time points from the data; otherwise it falls back to the default discharge‑time logic.
- **solver** (BaseSolver or None): optional solver to use; if None the Simulation’s default solver is used.
- **external_variables** (dict or None): optional dictionary of external variable values passed to the solver.
Outputs:
- Returns a ``pybamm.Solution`` instance stored in ``self.solution`` (also accessible via ``self._solution``). The solution’s time vector ``solution.t`` is in nondimensional units.
- May raise warnings of type ``pybamm.SolverWarning`` when ``t_eval`` does not contain all data points or when the maximum timestep in ``t_eval`` exceeds the minimum data timestep, but execution continues.
Description: Solves the built model for the specified ``t_eval`` (or automatically derived times when a drive‑cycle current is supplied). Includes validation of ``t_eval`` against drive‑cycle data and emits user warnings if the resolution may be insufficient.

Function: SolverWarning(message=None)
Location: pybamm/expression_tree/exceptions.py
Inputs:
- **message** (str, optional): custom warning message; if omitted a default message is used.
Outputs:
- An instance of ``UserWarning`` subclass that can be caught with ``assertWarns(pybamm.SolverWarning)``.
Description: Specialized warning emitted by solvers (especially when handling drive‑cycle data) to inform users about potential issues with the chosen ``t_eval`` resolution. It is a distinct warning type that can be filtered or tested.

#813 get t_eval from data
# Description
When using the `Simulation` class with the current provided as data (i..e drive cycles) `solve` now sets `t_eval` (if it isn't provided) to be the times in the data (non-dimensionlised). If `t_eval` is provided, `solve` checks that it contains all of the points in the data, and raises a warning if it doesn't. Maybe this should raise an actual exception to be totally fool proof, but there may be cases where people only want the solution returned at a subset of points. Happy for input on this. I think if people are solving in the long-winded way (i.e. not using `Simulation`) then we should just trust them to pick `t_eval` appropriately.

current.problem_statement:
fix t_eval to data for drive cycles
when simulating drive cycles the solvers work if `t_eval` is the same as the times provided in the data. when solving we should check if the current function has "[current data]" and then force the solve times to be those in the data (with a warning message that the solver is fixing t_eval). see below example

```
#
# Simulate drive cycle loaded from csv file
#
import pybamm
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import os

# load model
pybamm.set_logging_level("INFO")
model = pybamm.lithium_ion.DFN()

# create geometry
geometry = model.default_geometry

# get drive cycle data
cycle_name = "US06"
drive_cycle = pd.read_csv(
    os.path.join(pybamm.root_dir(), "input", "drive_cycles", cycle_name+".csv"),
    comment="#",
    skip_blank_lines=True
)
time_dim = drive_cycle.values[:, 0]
current_dim = drive_cycle.values[:, 1]

# load parameter values and process model and geometry
param = model.default_parameter_values
param["Current function [A]"] = "[current data]" + cycle_name
param.process_model(model)
param.process_geometry(geometry)

# set mesh
var = pybamm.standard_spatial_vars
var_pts = {var.x_n: 11, var.x_s: 11, var.x_p: 11, var.r_n: 5, var.r_p: 5}
mesh = pybamm.Mesh(geometry, model.default_submesh_types, var_pts)

# discretise model
disc = pybamm.Discretisation(mesh, model.default_spatial_methods)
disc.process_model(model)

# get dimensionless times for evaluation
tau = param.evaluate(pybamm.standard_parameters_lithium_ion.tau_discharge)
t_eval = time_dim / tau  # this works
# t_eval = np.linspace(0, 600 / tau, 600)  # this fails

# simulate US06 drive cycle
solver = pybamm.CasadiSolver(mode="fast")
solution = solver.solve(model, t_eval)

# plot
plot = pybamm.QuickPlot(solution)
plot.dynamic_plot()
```

Note that this works with Casadi in "fast" mode!

#813 get t_eval from data
# Description
When using the `Simulation` class with the current provided as data (i..e drive cycles) `solve` now sets `t_eval` (if it isn't provided) to be the times in the data (non-dimensionlised). If `t_eval` is provided, `solve` checks that it contains all of the points in the data, and raises a warning if it doesn't. Maybe this should raise an actual exception to be totally fool proof, but there may be cases where people only want the solution returned at a subset of points. Happy for input on this. I think if people are solving in the long-winded way (i.e. not using `Simulation`) then we should just trust them to pick `t_eval` appropriately. 

Fixes #813

current.problem_statement:
fix t_eval to data for drive cycles
when simulating drive cycles the solvers work if `t_eval` is the same as the times provided in the data. when solving we should check if the current function has "[current data]" and then force the solve times to be those in the data (with a warning message that the solver is fixing t_eval). see below example

```
#
# Simulate drive cycle loaded from csv file
#
import pybamm
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import os

# load model
pybamm.set_logging_level("INFO")
model = pybamm.lithium_ion.DFN()

# create geometry
geometry = model.default_geometry

# get drive cycle data
cycle_name = "US06"
drive_cycle = pd.read_csv(
    os.path.join(pybamm.root_dir(), "input", "drive_cycles", cycle_name+".csv"),
    comment="#",
    skip_blank_lines=True
)
time_dim = drive_cycle.values[:, 0]
current_dim = drive_cycle.values[:, 1]

# load parameter values and process model and geometry
param = model.default_parameter_values
param["Current function [A]"] = "[current data]" + cycle_name
param.process_model(model)
param.process_geometry(geometry)

# set mesh
var = pybamm.standard_spatial_vars
var_pts = {var.x_n: 11, var.x_s: 11, var.x_p: 11, var.r_n: 5, var.r_p: 5}
mesh = pybamm.Mesh(geometry, model.default_submesh_types, var_pts)

# discretise model
disc = pybamm.Discretisation(mesh, model.default_spatial_methods)
disc.process_model(model)

# get dimensionless times for evaluation
tau = param.evaluate(pybamm.standard_parameters_lithium_ion.tau_discharge)
t_eval = time_dim / tau  # this works
# t_eval = np.linspace(0, 600 / tau, 600)  # this fails

# simulate US06 drive cycle
solver = pybamm.CasadiSolver(mode="fast")
solution = solver.solve(model, t_eval)

# plot
plot = pybamm.QuickPlot(solution)
plot.dynamic_plot()
```

Note that this works with Casadi in "fast" mode!

#813 get t_eval from data
# Description
When using the `Simulation` class with the current provided as data (i..e drive cycles) `solve` now sets `t_eval` (if it isn't provided) to be the times in the data (non-dimensionlised). If `t_eval` is provided, `solve` checks that it contains all of the points in the data, and raises a warning if it doesn't. Maybe this should raise an actual exception to be totally fool proof, but there may be cases where people only want the solution returned at a subset of points. Happy for input on this. I think if people are solving in the long-winded way (i.e. not using `Simulation`) then we should just trust them to pick `t_eval` appropriately.

current.problem_statement:
fix t_eval to data for drive cycles
when simulating drive cycles the solvers work if `t_eval` is the same as the times provided in the data. when solving we should check if the current function has "[current data]" and then force the solve times to be those in the data (with a warning message that the solver is fixing t_eval). see below example

```
#
# Simulate drive cycle loaded from csv file
#
import pybamm
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import os

# load model
pybamm.set_logging_level("INFO")
model = pybamm.lithium_ion.DFN()

# create geometry
geometry = model.default_geometry

# get drive cycle data
cycle_name = "US06"
drive_cycle = pd.read_csv(
    os.path.join(pybamm.root_dir(), "input", "drive_cycles", cycle_name+".csv"),
    comment="#",
    skip_blank_lines=True
)
time_dim = drive_cycle.values[:, 0]
current_dim = drive_cycle.values[:, 1]

# load parameter values and process model and geometry
param = model.default_parameter_values
param["Current function [A]"] = "[current data]" + cycle_name
param.process_model(model)
param.process_geometry(geometry)

# set mesh
var = pybamm.standard_spatial_vars
var_pts = {var.x_n: 11, var.x_s: 11, var.x_p: 11, var.r_n: 5, var.r_p: 5}
mesh = pybamm.Mesh(geometry, model.default_submesh_types, var_pts)

# discretise model
disc = pybamm.Discretisation(mesh, model.default_spatial_methods)
disc.process_model(model)

# get dimensionless times for evaluation
tau = param.evaluate(pybamm.standard_parameters_lithium_ion.tau_discharge)
t_eval = time_dim / tau  # this works
# t_eval = np.linspace(0, 600 / tau, 600)  # this fails

# simulate US06 drive cycle
solver = pybamm.CasadiSolver(mode="fast")
solution = solver.solve(model, t_eval)

# plot
plot = pybamm.QuickPlot(solution)
plot.dynamic_plot()
```

Note that this works with Casadi in "fast" mode!

future.pr_description:
Issue 1006 process space var
# Description
Extend `processed_variable` to work in the case when `len(t_sol)=1` and also makes it so you no longer need to pass `t` to the call in the cases where the variable is constant (doesn't depend on `t` or `y`) or when `len(solution.t)=1` (e.g. algebraic models)

Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed. Please also include relevant motivation and context. List any dependencies that are required for this change.

Fixes #1006 and #571 

EDIT: Note that for variables discretised using finite elements (in y and z) the result returned by `ProcessedVariable` is transposed. This is consistent with other features, e.g. you can now do `plt.pcolormesh(x,y,z)` where `z` is some variable discretised with finite elements, whereas before you had to do `plt.pcolormesh(x,y,np.transpose(z))` 

## Type of change

Please add a line in the relevant section of [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) to document the change (include PR #) - note reverse order of PR #s. If necessary, also add to the list of breaking changes.

- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Optimization (back-end change that speeds up the code)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)


# Key checklist:

- [ ] No style issues: `$ flake8`
- [ ] All tests pass: `$ python run-tests.py --unit`
- [ ] The documentation builds: `$ cd docs` and then `$ make clean; make html`

You can run all three at once, using `$ python run-tests.py --quick`.

## Further checks:

- [ ] Code is commented, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] Tests added that prove fix is effective or that feature works

process space-only variables 
At the moment `ProcessedVariable` only works if `len(t)>1` (except for the special case of  2D finite elements, which can handle "fixed t" cases). It would be good to set it up so that any variables that are functions of space only can be processed.

current.interface:
Method: Simulation.solve(self, t_eval=None, solver=None, external_variables=None)
Location: pybamm/simulation.py
Inputs:
- **t_eval** (array‑like or None): optional array of nondimensional times at which the solution is requested. If None and the parameter *"Current function [A]"* is supplied via data (i.e., a tuple ``(filename, data)``), the method automatically uses the time points from the data; otherwise it falls back to the default discharge‑time logic.
- **solver** (BaseSolver or None): optional solver to use; if None the Simulation’s default solver is used.
- **external_variables** (dict or None): optional dictionary of external variable values passed to the solver.
Outputs:
- Returns a ``pybamm.Solution`` instance stored in ``self.solution`` (also accessible via ``self._solution``). The solution’s time vector ``solution.t`` is in nondimensional units.
- May raise warnings of type ``pybamm.SolverWarning`` when ``t_eval`` does not contain all data points or when the maximum timestep in ``t_eval`` exceeds the minimum data timestep, but execution continues.
Description: Solves the built model for the specified ``t_eval`` (or automatically derived times when a drive‑cycle current is supplied). Includes validation of ``t_eval`` against drive‑cycle data and emits user warnings if the resolution may be insufficient.

Function: SolverWarning(message=None)
Location: pybamm/expression_tree/exceptions.py
Inputs:
- **message** (str, optional): custom warning message; if omitted a default message is used.
Outputs:
- An instance of ``UserWarning`` subclass that can be caught with ``assertWarns(pybamm.SolverWarning)``.
Description: Specialized warning emitted by solvers (especially when handling drive‑cycle data) to inform users about potential issues with the chosen ``t_eval`` resolution. It is a distinct warning type that can be filtered or tested.

#813 get t_eval from data
# Description
When using the `Simulation` class with the current provided as data (i..e drive cycles) `solve` now sets `t_eval` (if it isn't provided) to be the times in the data (non-dimensionlised). If `t_eval` is provided, `solve` checks that it contains all of the points in the data, and raises a warning if it doesn't. Maybe this should raise an actual exception to be totally fool proof, but there may be cases where people only want the solution returned at a subset of points. Happy for input on this. current.problem_statement:
fix t_eval to data for drive cycles
when simulating drive cycles the solvers work if `t_eval` is the same as the times provided in the data. when solving we should check if the current function has "[current data]" and then force the solve times to be those in the data (with a warning message that the solver is fixing t_eval). see below example

```
#
# Simulate drive cycle loaded from csv file
#
import pybamm
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import os

# load model
pybamm.set_logging_level("INFO")
model = pybamm.lithium_ion.DFN()

# create geometry
geometry = model.default_geometry

# get drive cycle data
cycle_name = "US06"
drive_cycle = pd.read_csv(
    os.path.join(pybamm.root_dir(), "input", "drive_cycles", cycle_name+".csv"),
    comment="#",
    skip_blank_lines=True
)
time_dim = drive_cycle.values[:, 0]
current_dim = drive_cycle.values[:, 1]

# load parameter values and process model and geometry
param = model.default_parameter_values
param["Current function [A]"] = "[current data]" + cycle_name
param.process_model(model)
param.process_geometry(geometry)

# set mesh
var = pybamm.standard_spatial_vars
var_pts = {var.x_n: 11, var.x_s: 11, var.x_p: 11, var.r_n: 5, var.r_p: 5}
mesh = pybamm.Mesh(geometry, model.default_submesh_types, var_pts)

# discretise model
disc = pybamm.Discretisation(mesh, model.default_spatial_methods)
disc.process_model(model)

# get dimensionless times for evaluation
tau = param.evaluate(pybamm.standard_parameters_lithium_ion.tau_discharge)
t_eval = time_dim / tau  # this works
# t_eval = np.linspace(0, 600 / tau, 600)  # this fails

# simulate US06 drive cycle
solver = pybamm.CasadiSolver(mode="fast")
solution = solver.solve(model, t_eval)

# plot
plot = pybamm.QuickPlot(solution)
plot.dynamic_plot()
```

Note that this works with Casadi in "fast" mode!

current.problem_statement:
Bug when compiling with C when using variable `I`
### Describe the bug
When attempting to compile Python scripts using Pyccel with C, the process fails during the shared library generation stage when using the variable `I`. The error appears to be related to the handling of global variables in the generated C code. Could it be related to the imaginary unit `I`?

### To Reproduce

1. Clone git repo, setup virtual environment, and install Pyccel

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:pyccel/pyccel.git
cd pyccel

python3 -m venv env_pyccel
source env_pyccel/bin/activate
pip install .
```
2. Create two simple Python files (`test_I.py` and `test_J.py`) that define variables `J` and `I`, respectively.

```
echo "J=1" > test_J.py
echo "I=1" > test_I.py
```


3. Compile test_I.py and test_J.py with fortran and C.

```
pyccel test_J.py --language=fortran
pyccel test_J.py --language=c
pyccel test_I.py --language=fortran
pyccel test_I.py --language=c
```

The three first tests work fine for me, but I get an error on the fourth.

### Error details
The error occurs specifically when compiling `test_I.py` with C.

future.problem_statement:
Allow iterating over a set
### Describe the feature
It should be possible to iterate over a set.

### Test Code
Provide code which does not currently work but which should do when this issue is fixed:
```python
a = {1,3,4}
sum_a = 0
for ai in a:
     sum_a += ai
```

### Proposed Solution
This should be implemented using `IteratorType` and `Iterable`. The code should be flexible enough to make it easy to do the same for dicts (dict_keys/dict_values) later.

In C the code should be:
```c
c_for_each(Dummy_0000, set_int, a)
{
    ai = *Dummy_0000.ref;
    sum_a += ai;
}
```
In Fortran the code should be:
```fortran
      iter = a % begin()
      last = a % end()
      do while (iter /= last)
         ai = iter%of()
         sum_a = sum_a + ai
         call iter%next()
      end do
```
